question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}s-\frac{2}{3}t=-1 \\ s+\frac{1}{4}t=2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $4,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}s-\frac{2}{3}t=-1 & |\times 3 \\ s+\frac{1}{4}t=2 & |\times 4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}5s-2t=-3 \\ 4s+t=8\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the second equation can easily be solved for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4s+t & =8 \\ t & =8-4s\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $t=8-4s$ into the first equation and then solve for $s:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5s-2t & =-3 \\ 5s-2(8-4s) & =-3 \\ 5s-16+8s & =-3 \\ 13s & =13 \\ s & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $t,$ we substitute $s=1$ into the equation $t=8-4s$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =8-4s \\  & =8-4(1) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $s=1$ and $t=4.$
